steps.title: The API entry point
steps.text: `app/main.py` creates the FastAPI app and mounts routers from `app/routes/`. The web app calls it under `/api/v1`; auth is a bearer token checked in `app/deps.py`.
steps.narration: Everything starts at the FastAPI app, which the web client calls over REST.

steps.title: Postgres through SQLAlchemy
steps.text: Models live in `app/models.py`. Each request gets an `AsyncSession` from `get_db`. Alembic migrations are in `migrations/versions/` and run on container start.
steps.narration: The API reads and writes Postgres through async SQLAlchemy sessions.

steps.title: How a request gets a session
steps.text: `get_db` is a FastAPI dependency. The session commits when the route returns and rolls back if it raises, so routes never call `commit()` themselves.
steps.narration: One dependency owns the transaction for each request.

visual.code:
async def get_db() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
    async with SessionLocal() as session:
        try:
            yield session
            await session.commit()
        except Exception:
            await session.rollback()
            raise

steps.title: Slow work goes to a worker
steps.text: Charging a card takes seconds, so `POST /orders` stores the order as `pending` and enqueues `charge_order`. Redis is the Celery broker.
steps.narration: The API hands slow payment work to a Celery worker through Redis.

steps.title: The worker charges and updates
steps.text: `charge_order` calls Stripe, then sets the order to `paid` or `failed` in Postgres. It retries three times on network errors with exponential backoff.
steps.narration: The worker talks to Stripe and writes the outcome back to the database.

steps.title: What runs locally
steps.text: `docker compose up` starts the API, worker, Postgres and Redis. Stripe stays external; local runs use the test key from `.env.example`.
steps.narration: Four containers run locally. Stripe is the only outside dependency.
